classification.difficultyReason: Recognise the diameters as diagonals and use their equality, bisection and perpendicularity to justify the quadrilateral classifications.

children.label: a
children.prompt: In the diagram to the right, $O$ is the centre of the circle, and $AB$ and $FG$ are diameters of the circle. What sort of figure is $AFBG$, and why?

spec.description: Two oblique diameters AB and FG intersect at the marked centre O. AB slopes slightly down to the right; FG slopes more steeply down to the right. The quadrilateral sides remain undrawn. Ordinary source blue lines are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: A and B are opposite endpoints of one diameter; F and G are opposite endpoints of another diameter of the same circle.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied diameters, circle, centre and labels are visible; no classification or quadrilateral sides are added.

answer.short: $AFBG$ is a rectangle: its diagonals $AB$ and $FG$ are equal and bisect each other.
answer.worked:
$OA=OB=OF=OG$, since all four lengths are radii of the same circle. Hence $AB=FG$, and $O$ is the midpoint of both diameters.

The diagonals of $AFBG$ are therefore equal and bisect each other, so $AFBG$ is a rectangle.

children.label: b
children.prompt: In the diagram to the right, $O$ is the centre of the circle, and $AB$ and $FG$ are perpendicular diameters of the circle. What sort of figure is $AFBG$, and why?

spec.description: Vertical diameter AB and horizontal diameter FG intersect at the marked centre O. A right-angle square occupies the sector between OA and OG. The quadrilateral sides remain undrawn. Ordinary source blue lines are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: AB and FG are perpendicular diameters of the same circle, with A above B and F left of G.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied circle, perpendicular diameters, right-angle marker, centre and labels are visible.

answer.short: $AFBG$ is a square: its diagonals are equal and bisect each other at right angles.
answer.worked:
$OA=OB=OF=OG$, since all four lengths are radii of the same circle. Thus $AB=FG$, and the diagonals bisect each other at $O$.

Equal diagonals that bisect each other show that $AFBG$ is a rectangle. Since these diagonals also meet at right angles, $AFBG$ is a rhombus.

Being both a rectangle and a rhombus, $AFBG$ is a square.
